prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the exact same line in src/mcp/server/stdio.py — the buffer_size argument passed when constructing the write_stream memory object stream for the stdio server transport. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks union args against a literal frozenset of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}, but does not unwrap Annotated — so the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern (used throughout this SDK's own docs for describing optional string params) still fails the 'is simple type' check and remains subject to the same corruption bug it's meant to fix. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before comparing union members, so Field-annotated optional strings are correctly skipped from pre-parsing. #2032's broader coverage of non-None simple-type unions (str|int, str|bool, etc.) is a real advantage not preserved by #3056 alone, so whichever PR is kept should ideally incorporate #2032's SIMPLE_TYPES generalization on top of #3056's Annotated-unwrapping, but as submitted #3056 fixes the more common real-world case.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError and its subclasses (notably UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to pickle/unpickle correctly — the default Exception.__reduce__ calls cls(*self.args), but MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None). This raises TypeError on unpickle (tracked as issue #2431, referenced explicitly by #2555). (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError and its subclasses (notably UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to pickle/unpickle correctly — the default Exception.__reduce__ calls cls(*self.args), but MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None). prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 fixes this generically at the MCPError base class via __reduce__ = (_restore_mcp_error, (type(self), self.args), self.__dict__), using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restoration. clusters.desc: Concurrent POST requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id both route through `_request_streams` keyed by that id, so the second request silently overwrites the first's slot and cross-wires responses (referenced as issue #3060 in #3063's own commit message). Both PRs add a rejection path for a duplicate in-flight id. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks union args against a literal frozenset of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}, but does not unwrap Annotated — so the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern (used throughout this SDK's own docs for describing optional string params) still fails the 'is simple type' check and remains subject to the same corruption bug it's meant to fix. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before comparing union members, so Field-annotated optional strings are correctly skipped from pre-parsing. #2032's broader coverage of non-None simple-type unions (str|int, str|bool, etc.) is a real advantage not preserved by #3056 alone, so whichever PR is kept should ideally incorporate #2032's SIMPLE_TYPES generalization on top of #3056's Annotated-unwrapping, but as submitted #3056 fixes the more common real-world case.

members.title: Fix stateless HTTP task accumulation causing memory leak
members.author: wiggzz

members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both modify the exact same line in src/mcp/server/stdio.py — the buffer_size argument passed when constructing the write_stream memory object stream for the stdio server transport. members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3262: MCPError and its subclasses (notably UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to pickle/unpickle correctly — the default Exception.__reduce__ calls cls(*self.args), but MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None). This raises TypeError on unpickle (tracked as issue #2431, referenced explicitly by #2555).

members.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 fixes this generically at the MCPError base class via __reduce__ = (_restore_mcp_error, (type(self), self.args), self.__dict__), using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ restoration. This sidesteps subclass constructor signatures entirely, so it covers UrlElicitationRequiredError and any other/future MCPError subclass without special-casing, and its test diff adds coverage for an additional subclass (NoBackChannelError) alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError. #2555 only defines __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself (cls(self._elicitations, self.message)), so it fixes just that one subclass and leaves any other non-conforming MCPError subclass broken. #2478 also attempts a base-class fix via a _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) helper, but its shown diff only defines the helper without wiring it into any __reduce__ method, and its approach still hardcodes an if/else special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError.from_error vs the generic from_error_data path — less extensible than 3262's fully generic dict-restoring reconstruction, and its wiring/completeness is unverifiable from the diff.

clusters.pick_reason: Goes further than #3252's fix (which still keeps a single anyio.Lock, just releases it before yielding the response) and further than #2858 (same narrow-the-critical-section approach) by replacing anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1) — anyio.Lock enforces same-task release, but httpx can resume/close the auth-flow async generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which is a correctness gap #2858 and #3252 don't address. It also splits locking into a dedicated flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions versus the general lock for normal requests, giving finer-grained concurrency than either single-lock alternative.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 guards using `request_id in self._request_streams` where request_id is already `str(message.id)`, so a numeric id `1` and string id "1" collapse to the same key — it can false-positive a 409 on an unrelated id, and a string id equal to the literal "_GET_stream" would collide with the reserved standalone GET slot. #3221 replaces the lookup with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes by JSON-RPC type (`i:`/`s:`) before comparing, which preserves the int/string distinction and structurally can't collide with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing both gaps #3063 leaves open.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent POST requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id both route through `_request_streams` keyed by that id, so the second request silently overwrites the first's slot and cross-wires responses (referenced as issue #3060 in #3063's own commit message). Both PRs add a rejection path for a duplicate in-flight id.
